study_identification_part.si4_title: Lifespan Normative Modeling of Brain Microstructure

study_characteristics_part.sc1_study_objective: To develop the first large-scale normative model of brain white matter (WM) microstructure across the human lifespan using 19 international diffusion MRI datasets, and to illustrate its utility in detecting WM microstructural deviations in various neurological and neurogenetic conditions.

rci7_preprocessing_pipeline.answer: Software: DiPy (tensor fitting); FSL (dtifit, flirt); ANTs (diffeomorphic non-linear registration); 3DMI (non-linear registration for QTIM). Steps: Eddy current, movement, EPI-induced susceptibility distortion correction; tensor fitting; linear and non-linear registration to ENIGMA-FA template. Atlas: Johns Hopkins University WM atlas (JHU-WM) using ENIGMA-DTI protocol for 22 ROIs (21 bilateral regions + Global-WM).
rci7_preprocessing_pipeline.reason: The 'Preprocessing of diffusion MRI scans' section provides a comprehensive description of the software, processing steps, and atlases used in the pipeline.
rci7_preprocessing_pipeline.supporting_text: Three studies provided preprocessed dMRI images... The remaining datasets were preprocessed in-house. In all cases, preprocessing included correction for eddy currents, movement, and EPI-induced susceptibility distortions... DTI maps (FA, MD, RD and AD) were computed with DiPy's tensor fitting function... FSL's dtifit was used to fit the diffusion tensor... All subjects' FA maps were linearly registered with FSL's flirt and nonlinearly registered to the ENIGMA-FA template with ANTs' diffeomorphic non-linear registration algorithm... For QTIM, nonlinear registration was performed using the 3DMI algorithm... Mean DTI metrics were extracted from 21 bilateral regions of interest (regions) from the Johns Hopkins University WM atlas (JHU-WM) using the ENIGMA-DTI protocol.
rci7_preprocessing_pipeline.location: VillalonReina2024.pdf.md: 2. Preprocessing of diffusion MRI scans

rci8_quality_checking.detail: Manual QC for head movement, FOV artifacts, and preprocessing errors applied to ADNI3, OASIS3, PPMI, CAMCAN, HBN. Automated outlier detection for other datasets using isolation forests (Scikit-learn) on each ROI/DTI metric; subjects identified as outliers in at least two DTI metrics were removed. Total 54,583 subjects remained after QC.
rci8_quality_checking.supporting_text: ADNI3, OASIS3, PPMI, CAMCAN and HBN were manually checked for head movement, FOV (field of view) related artifacts and other dMRI acquisition artifacts and preprocessing errors... For all other datasets used for training, outliers were detected with an anomaly detection algorithm called isolation forests implemented in Scikit-learn... outlier subjects that were duplicated in at least two DTI metrics were removed from the sample. Aggregating the subjects left after this procedure plus the subjects from the datasets that were manually checked, a total of 54,583 subjects remained for training.

rci9_site_effect_handling.detail: Hierarchical Bayesian Regression (HBR) was used to model site, scanner, and cohort effects by treating dMRI acquisition protocol as a batch effect. HBR is a partial pooling strategy where parameters are estimated separately for each batch, and Z-scores are adjusted for additive and multiplicative batch effects. Age was a fixed independent variable, and sex was a second grouping variable. The approach aims to preserve biological variability correlated with batch effects.
rci9_site_effect_handling.supporting_text: Here we address this challenge using hierarchical Bayesian regression (HBR) 16, an approach designed to model site, scanner and cohort effects in multi-site data... we used the dMRI protocol as the batch effect when training the normative model with HBR. HBR models these site-dependent parameters in a hyperprior... The harmonization of Z-scores happens at this stage where the Z-scores are adjusted for additive and multiplicative batch effects using the estimated µ and σ for each batch... it preserves the sources of biological variability that may correlate with the batch effects.

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa7_association_analysis: Classification accuracy using ROI-wise Area Under the ROC Curve (AUC) with permutation tests and FDR correction for patient vs. control discrimination; Spearman correlations to test 'gain-predicts-loss' hypothesis (percent change from age 4 to peak vs. peak to age 91); Assessment of associations between percent change (age 4-14, 75-85, 85-91) and age of peak to test 'last-in, first-out' hypothesis; Pairwise comparisons with repeated measures ANOVA (percentile bootstrap method) for average age of peak across regions between DTI metrics.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa8_key_findings_brief: The study successfully developed and validated a large-scale lifespan normative model of brain white matter microstructure using HBR, demonstrating its utility in detecting and characterizing individual-level microstructural deviations in mild cognitive impairment, Alzheimer's disease, and 22q11.2 deletion syndrome.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa9_key_findings_detailed: Lifespan trajectories for Global-WM showed an inverted U-shaped trajectory for FA (peak at 29 years) and U-shaped trajectories for MD (minimum at 43 years), RD (minimum at 37 years), and AD (minimum at 53 years). In anomaly detection, for dementia, highest AUCs were observed for CGH RD (0.74), MD (0.7), and FA (0.65), and BCC AD (0.67). For MCI, AUCs ranged from 0.55-0.6, with best performance for SCC MD (0.6), BCC AD (0.67), and FX FA/MD (0.58/0.59). Most extreme deviations in dementia/MCI were positive for diffusivities (MD, RD, AD) and negative for FA. RD showed the largest proportion of extreme deviations (e.g., 37% dementia in CGH). Model adaptation to NIMHANS showed greater severity in MCI than dementia, with extreme positive deviations for MD, AD, RD in MCI. For dementia, all four DTI metrics showed significant extreme deviations. In 22qDel (UCLA), significant effects were found in MD (9/21 regions) and AD (5/21 regions), primarily negative extreme deviations, except for PLIC AD (positive). The 'gain-predicts-loss' hypothesis was not supported. Some evidence supported the 'last-in first-out' hypothesis for MD (Rho=0.47, p=0.03), indicating a correlation between faster decrease of MD (age 4-14) and younger age of minimum MD.

caa10_key_limitations.answer: ENIGMA-DTI protocol not optimized for very early childhood (3-5 years); potential CSF contamination in some regions (e.g., fornix) due to partial volume effects/misregistration; reliance on DTI as a non-specific microstructural model; single-shell scanning protocols limit advanced multi-compartmental models; potential benefit from more advanced distributional models (e.g., non-Gaussian, nonlinear probability warping, SHASH, high-dimensional VAEs).
caa10_key_limitations.supporting_text: One limitation of this study is that the ENIGMA-DTI protocol has not been optimized for very early childhood (3-5 years)... Some regions, such as the fornix, may be contaminated with cerebrospinal fluid due to partial volume effects caused by misregistration to the ENIGMA template... Although our results presented are based on DTI, the reference models are still highly sensitive... Additionally, the single-shell scanning protocols are, to this day, the most commonly available on most MRI scanners. More advanced multi-compartmental models beyond DTI will require multi-shell dMRI data... Finally, more advanced distributional models may also be beneficial for normative modeling...

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa11_application_notes: Large-scale normative models offer transdiagnostic clinical value by yielding individual anomaly profiles, agnostic to clinical labels, addressing heterogeneity within clinical groups. The anomaly detection framework can gauge disease severity in new subjects via model adaptation. It also revealed opposing deviations in subgroups (e.g., 22qDel), which would be missed by group average approaches.
